facts.statement: The genus Brasilosuchus was named by Souza-Filho and Bocquentin-Villanueva in 1989.
The only known species, Brasilosuchus mendesi, was named by Jonas Souza-Filho and Jean Bocquentin-Villanueva in 1989.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Brasilosuchus mendesi, named by Jonas Souza-Filho and Jean Bocquentin-Villanueva in 1989.

facts.statement: Researchers later tentatively re-identified the animal as a species of Charactosuchus in an unpublished 1993 conference abstract.
facts.quote: They subsequently re-identified it as a species of Charactosuchus in a 1993 conference abstract, but this conclusion has not been accepted since it was not published.

facts.statement: Brasilosuchus was an extinct crocodilian that lived in Brazil during the Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: Brasilosuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of crocodilian that lived during the Miocene of Brazil.

facts.statement: It is possible that Brasilosuchus belongs to the subfamily Tomistominae, though this has not been confirmed by phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Along with Charactosuchus, it is possibly a member of Tomistominae, but they have not been included in a phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Brasilosuchus date from the Tortonian stage, between 11.63 and 7.246 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Tortonian (11.63 to 7.246 million years ago)

facts.statement: Brasilosuchus is classified within the superfamily Crocodyloidea.
Brasilosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Brasilosuchus is Brasilosuchus mendesi.
